Our Story

Every piece is set by hand, one stone at a time

Marathmola Saj began with a simple idea — Maharashtrian bridal jewellery shouldn't have to be mass-produced to be affordable. Every nath, pearl strand and jhumka you see here is hand-wired, hand-strung and hand-set in our small workshop, using traditional kundan and pearl-setting techniques passed down through generations.

We make each order fresh, so sizing, stone colour and pearl tone can all be adjusted to you.

Our Craft

From wire to worn, in four steps

Nothing here is cast in bulk. Each piece moves through the same hands from raw wire and loose stone to the finished set you receive.

1

Design & sizing

We confirm the motif, stone colour and nath/necklace sizing with you before work begins.

2

Hand-wiring

Gold-tone wire is shaped and filigreed by hand into the base motif — no moulds, no casting.

3

Stone & pearl setting

Kundan stones and pearls are set and strung individually, checked for symmetry at every step.

4

Finishing & packing

Each piece is polished, quality-checked and packed for travel before it leaves the workshop.
